$note: Hand-written. Everything else under corpus/ is captured or generated. See corpus/manifest.ts for what each field guarantees, and docs/TANK01.md for how to add a game.

games.why: The baseline. An ordinary, high-profile game with nothing rare in it, so a translator change that breaks everyday scoring cannot hide behind the edge cases.
A blocked field goal that led to no score at all. 27 of 2025's 44 blocked kicks did not score, and every one of them was invisible until teamStats was read.
The verbose safety wording, 'Defensive Holding in Endzone for Safety', which shares no tokens with the terse form and is the reason safeties are counted from scoreType rather than parsed.
Marcus Jones's punt return: a special-teams touchdown by a defensive player, so DST.defTD already holds it and adding one from the text pays the unit twice.
'Marshawn Kneeland Blocked Punt Recovery in End Zone' — a special-teams touchdown with no 'return' anywhere in it, which the old pattern scored as nothing.
Rashid Shaheed's punt return, where Tank01 orders playerIDs [passer, returner, receiver] — the ordering that paid a quarterback six points for a punt return.
The only scoreType 'BP' in two seasons. Twelve points on one play, paid to nobody, and neither provider counter made it up.

espnTypeDisagreements.text: Hunter Long 22 Yd Return of Blocked Punt (Joshua Karty Kick)
espnTypeDisagreements.reason: The only scoreType 'BP' in two seasons, and ESPN leaves scoringType null on the same play — so 'BP' appears to be Tank01's own filing for a play ESPN declines to type rather than a value ESPN publishes.

games.why: J.J. Russell's blocked-punt return: playerIDs holds the kicker alone and Russell's whole record is a snapCounts block. Also both open-ended bottom tiers.
All four field-goal buckets in one game including a 65-yarder, an abbreviated name in the play text, and the terse safety wording.
George Holani's recovered kickoff: a coverage score ESPN pays the player 0 for and Sleeper pays 6, plus two identical field-goal texts and an ESPN play with no scoringType.

espnTypeDisagreements.text: George Holani Recovered Kickoff in End Zone for a Touchdown (Jason Myers Kick)
espnTypeDisagreements.reason: ESPN leaves scoringType null and files the play under stat id 104, its fumble-return touchdown; Tank01 types it TD. The one play in the corpus where the two feeds put different labels on the same sentence.

games.why: A shutout and under 100 yards allowed: the top tier of both defensive ladders, neither of which any other corpus game reaches.
A fumble-recovery touchdown as a negative case — it must pay the unit def_td and must never reach the scorer as ret_td.

A two-point conversion whose receiver, Julian Hill, is absent from playerIDs and has no category block of his own. box-score.ts resolves him from the parenthetical text and the ledger credits him, so this is the fixture that would notice that text path being removed. Refs #155, which stays open for the conversions the text does not name.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:SF
knownDisagreements.reason: Points allowed. Arizona scored 15 including a safety; Tank01 charges San Francisco's unit all 15 and Sleeper charges 13. Sleeper excludes a safety from points allowed and ESPN does not. We follow ESPN because the whole scoring table came from ESPN.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:CAR
knownDisagreements.reason: Points allowed, same convention as PHI@TB. New England scored 42 including Marcus Jones's punt return; ESPN subtracts 6 for it and charges Carolina 36, Sleeper charges the full 42. Both readings land in the same tier here, so the two units are paid identically — which is exactly why this one was invisible until the comparison was made on stats rather than on totals.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:TB
knownDisagreements.reason: Points allowed, the other direction. Philadelphia scored 31 including Sydney Brown's blocked-punt return; ESPN subtracts 6 for it (not 7 — the extra point still counts) and charges Tampa 25, Sleeper charges the full 31.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:PHI
knownDisagreements.reason: Points allowed, the safety direction, in the same game as the dst:TB entry above. Tampa scored 25 including a safety; Sleeper excludes a safety from points allowed and charges 23, ESPN does not and charges 25. Same tier either way, so the totals agree and only the stat differs.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:PIT
knownDisagreements.reason: The same convention as PHI@TB. Seattle scored 31 including George Holani's recovered kickoff; ESPN subtracts 6 and charges Pittsburgh 25, Sleeper charges 31.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:SEA
knownDisagreements.reason: Tank01 reports DST.defTD 4 for two fumble-recovery touchdowns, all four on DeMarcus Lawrence's own Defense.defTD. teamStats says 2 and Sleeper says 2. We pay Seattle 24 points where 12 are due. The existing cross-check already fires with an arithmetically impossible negative count and nothing refuses the value.

knownDisagreements.subject: dst:ARI
knownDisagreements.reason: The same wrong count reaching the other unit. ESPN derives points allowed as the opponent's score minus 6 per defensive touchdown, so Seattle's 44 becomes 20 against the four it believes in and 32 against the two that happened. def_pts_allowed is tiered, so this is a tier boundary as well as a number.

unjoinable.name: George Holani
unjoinable.reason: Tank01's player list gives him sleeperBotID 8063, which is George Silvanic. The surname check in the capture refuses the pair rather than comparing two different people, so his line in 20251109_ARI@SEA is not checked against Sleeper at all.
